proof.negativeControl: On main the same test cannot run (`processes.retireTreeProcesses is not a function`, the Task 1 red run); behaviourally, the existing sibling `lets a root's own self-report POST to /process/exit resolve…` shows main's contract: only closeTree stops the pane and the tree ends `closed`, never lingering with a kept session file. In the scratch run above, main left every pane alive after linger.

trickyParts: The retire summary line is logged from `retireTreeProcesses` (the linger entry point), not the shared primitive: a close stays as quiet as before (an existing test pins that a close of an already-reaped pane logs nothing), while every linger retire logs exactly one line.

`closeTreeLocked` re-marks `lingering` with `lingerUntil = now` only on a `StopFailed` from the primitive; any other rejection (the primitive's own persist failing) propagates untouched, which keeps the `marks a tree lingering as its first durable act` crash test at exactly two saves.
The root leg is awaited before the worker leg (as before), so a test holding shutdown frames must release them one at a time.

`reportRootExit` on a tree still `active` (the linger effect never reached it — an issue.updated carrying done emits none) lingers it first with a real linger window instead of leaving an active record with no locator, no slot, and nothing probing it; this is what makes the architect's accepted statement ("leaves the tree lingering until lingerUntil") true in that edge too.

api.test.ts and api.thermo-auth.test.ts seeded the registering root `queued`; a launched tree is `active` (admit()/spawnTree write it before any pane exists), so the seeds now say `active` and the route's redundant `status = "active"` write is gone.

The LEGION-163 index test polled a silent 20k-tick budget across real workspace-removal I/O and failed once under the box's load average of 120 during the whole-suite gate; it and the two new index tests now await the teardown's own persist (the event) instead. `capturingErrors` was hoisted to module scope in processes.test.ts so the new describes could use it.
deviations: Task 6's `secrets DISPATCH_TOKEN GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 … --` launch line does not apply on this box: the deployment's daemon reads App keys through `private_key_command: cat /etc/legion/*.pem` (readable by uid legion) and Dispatch credentials from the operator's envoy.json; the scratch daemon used the same private_key_command and an unroutable DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN so nothing real was written. No `secrets` CLI exists on this box.

The scratch seeds' roots hold no daemon-minted capability, so their fixtures' /process/exit answered 403 (recorded in l-result/a-result); the 200 round trip is proven by the real-tmux E2E test instead. The panes were stopped and the state cleared exactly as the acceptance asks regardless.

isTreeGone treating `lingering` like `closed`, reportRootExit retiring instead of closing, /process/exit routing a lingering root to reportRootExit whatever the issue status, and the `while retiring the processes of` log wording — all as the architect accepted in the assignment.
